text.p: The lira closed easier at 105,780 against the dollar on Thursday after Wednesday's 105,530 due to banks' dollar demand despite central bank's limited dollar sales to a few banks, bankers said.
Bankers said sellers were weak in the currency market and the lira which opened at 105,750, weakened to 105,960 at midday on banks' dollar demand.
The central bank sold dollars for lira in early afternoon to meet the demand, causing the lira to firm to 105,780 at close.
The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers at 105,450 lira at the opening, after Wednesday's 105,200 lira close.
The money market opened with a 44.4 trillion lira surplus.

Overnight money rates sank to 57.25 percent from 77.75 in the morning and the central bank drained 7.1 trillion lira at 57 percent overnight at close. It had lent 1.3 trillion lira at 78 percent yesterday when the average money rate was 77.77 pct.

The central bank also lent banks 28.4 trillion lira via t/n value deals at 74 percent, down from the 32.3 trillion lira it funded on Wednesday. It also lent 850 bln lira at 75 percent via tomorrow/week value deals.

Bond market yields firmed around half a point in correction after the recent sharp falls. Yields had dived by some five points across the board on a buying spree prompted by strong demand and sharp yield cut in the Treasury's 13-month bond auction on Tuesday.

The average yield on the most heavily traded January 14, 1998 paper firmed to 110.16 percent from Wednesday's 109.71. The second most active September 3, 1997 paper yielded 111.71, up from Wednesday's 111.53 percent average.
